sections.description:
Short title, extent and commencement

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
1. Short title, extent and commencement.--(1) This Order may be called
the Hoarding and Black Market Order, 1956.
(2) It extends to Federal
Capital.
(3) It shall come into force at
once.

In this Order, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
2. In this Order, unless there is anything
repugnant in the subject or context,--
(1) "Government" means
the Central Government;
(2) "dealing
in the black market" means; .
(3) otherwise
than in accordance with any Pakistan
law--
(i) selling, bartering, exchanging,
supplying or disposing of article rationed by or under any such law;
(ii) supplying
distributing, selling, disposing of or parting with the possession or custody
of, or offering to supply, distribute, sell, barter, exchange, dispose of or
part with the possession or custody of or acquiring or taking into possession
anything the supply, distribution, sale, barter, exchange, disposal, parting
with the possession or custody, acquiring or taking into possession of which is
by or under any such law prohibited or subject to any restrictions or
conditions whether of price or otherwise;
(iii) producing, manufacturing, or treating anything the
production, manufacture or treatment of which is subject to restriction or
conditions imposed by or under any such law;
(iv) moving or
purporting to sell, barter, exchange or supply or purporting to acquire or take
not possession for the purpose of trade anything vested in Government by or
under any law for the time being in force;
(v) using of dealing with any licence,
permit or ration document issued by or under any such law;
(b) making,
uttering or using any counterfeit or forged licence,
permit or ration document purporting to be a licence,
permit or ration document duly granted or issued under any Pakistan law;
(c) in contravention of a prohibition, restriction or direction
imposed in that behalf by or under any Pakistan law;
(ii)
withholding anything from sale; or
(d) selling or buying anything for purpose of trade at a price
greater than the maximum price fixed by or under any Pakistan law;
(3) "hoarding" means
stocking or storing anything in excess of the maximum quantity of that thing
allowed to be held in stock or storage at any one time by any person by under
any Pakistan law; and
(4) "Special Judge"
means a person appointed as such under this Order.

Punishment for hoarding or dealing in black market

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
3. Punishment for hoarding or dealing in black market.--(1) Whoever
is found guilty of the offence of hoarding or dealing in the black market
shall, notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any other enactment for the
time being in force, be punishable‑
(a) if the
offence is tried summarily, with imprisonment which extend to one year but
shall not, except for reasons to be recorded, be less than six months, and with
fine; and
(b) if the
offence is not tried summarily, imprisonment which may extend to seven years
but shall not except for reasons to be recorded, be less than not one year, and
with fine:
Provided that if
in the case of an offence of hoarding, the person accused of Such offence proves
that he was hoarding for purposes other than gain, whether, financial
or otherwise, he shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to six
months or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees or with both.
(2) A Court convicting any person
of an offence of hoarding or dealing in the black market shall order the
forfeiture to the Government of anything in respect or which the offence was
committed, or, where such forfeiture is impossible then forfeiture of an
equivalent quantity of the like thing belonging to such person, or may order
such person, notwithstanding any fine that may be imposed upon him under this
Article, to forfeit the equivalent in money or such things assessed at the date
of order of forfeiture.
sections.punishment:
punishable with imprisonment which may extend to six
months or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees or with both.

sections.description:
Prohibition of carrying on business in certain cases

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
4. Prohibition of carrying on business in certain cases.--(1) On
the third or any subsequent occasion on which a person is convicted of an
offence under the Order the Government may makes an order, having effect during
such period as it thinks fit to fix, forbidding the convicted with the carrying
on of the business in the course of which the offence was committed, or any
branch of that business or any business or branch of a business of a similar
character.
(2) Whoever contravenes an order
under this Article shall be punishable with imprisonment of either description
for a term which may extend to six months and with fine.
sections.punishment:
punishable with imprisonment of either description
for a term which may extend to six months and with fine.

sections.description:
Vicarious Liability

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
5. Vicarious Liability.--(1) Where an offence of hoarding or
dealing in the black market is committed-‑
(a) by a body corporate every director, manager, secretary or
other officer or servant, or
(b) by a firm, every partner, secretary, principal
officer and every agent of the partnership, or
(c) by a joint Hindu family business, the karta,
every adult member, manager, gomasta, agent or
servant;
shall, if actively concerned in
the conduct of the business of such body, firm, or joint
Hindu family, be deemed to have committed the offence unless he proves that the
offence was committed without his knowledge and that he used all due diligence
to prevent the commission of the offence.
(2) The provisions of Article 12
shall apply to any offence referred to in clause (1) of this Article.
(3) Where a karta,
adult member, manager, gomasta, agent or servant of a
joint Hindu family business is fined that fine shall be realisable
from his personal property and also from the assets of the joint family.

Attempts and abetments

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
6. Attempts and abetments.--Any person who attempts to commit an
offence under this Order, or abets or attempts to abet the commission of such
an offence, shall be deemed to have committed that offence:
Provided that
the buying of goods for a purpose other than that of trade shall not by itself
amount to abetment of the offence of dealing in the black market.

Abetment by public servants

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
7. Abetment by public servants.-- An public servants as defined
in the Pakistan Penal Code (XLV of 1860) who by a dereliction of duty d
facilitates the commission by any person of an offence of hoarding or dealing
in the black market shall be deemed to have abetted the commission of the said
offence with the meaning of Article 6.

Bond by convicted person

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
8. Bond by convicted person.--(1) The Court on convicting any
person under this Order may in addition to any punishment to which he may be sentenced
thereunder, order him to execute a bond for a sum
proportionate to his means, with or without sureties, to be of good behaviour for a period not exceeding three years.
(2) If he fails to execute the
bonds on or before the date on which the period for which the bond is to be
given commences, the Court may order him to be committed to prison, or, if he
is already in prison, to be detained in prison, until he executes the bond, and
such detention shall, if the punishment referred to in clause (1) includes a
term of imprisonment, commence to the expiration of that term, but shall in no
case exceed twelve months.
(3) If having executed the bond
he commits any breach of any condition in the bond the bond shall forthwith
stand forfeited, and he, and in his default any other person bound by the bond
as surety, shall pay the penalty thereof.
Provided that if
the person executing the bond shows cause to the satisfaction of the Court why
such penalty should not be levied from him it shall not be levied from him or
from any surety to the bond.
(4) Imprisonment for failure to
execute the bond shall be simple.

Bond for good behaviour in creation cases

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
9. Bond for good behaviour in creation
cases.--(1) Whoever the District Magistrate, of Karachi or a Magistrate of
the first class specially empowered in this behalf, has information that there
is within the limits of his jurisdiction any person who within, or without such
limits transports foodstuff in contravention of an order made or deemed to have
been made under the Control of Essential Commodities Ordinance, 1956 (III of
1956), or the Federal Capital (Essential Supplies) Order, 1956 (III of 1956) he
may, if in his opinion there is sufficient ground for proceeding, require such
person to show cause why he should not be ordered to execute a bond with or without
sureties for his good behaviour for such period not
exceeding be year as the Magistrate thinks fit to fix, and upon the execution
of such bond the Provisions of Chapter VIII and XLII of the Code of Criminal
Procedure, 1898, (V of 1898), shall apply to the case.
(2) Any contravention of an order
made or deemed to have been made Linder the aforesaid Ordinance or Order, by
such person after the execution of such bond shall be deemed to constitute a
forfeiture of the bond.

Arrest and bail

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
10. Arrest and bail.--Any offence punishable under this Order shall
be cognizable and, accept as provided in Article 11 bail shall not be granted
for an offence punishable under this Order accept in, provided in Sections 497 and 498 of the Code
of Criminal Procedure, 1898, for the grant of bail in case of Non-bailable offence.
sections.punishment:
punishable under this Order shall
be cognizable and, accept as provided in Article 11 bail shall not be granted
for an offence punishable under this Order accept in, provided in Sections 497 and 498 of the Code
of Criminal Procedure, 1898, for the grant of bail in case of Non-bailable offence.

sections.description:
Special provision regarding ball

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
11. Special provision regarding ball.--Notwithstanding anything
contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (V of 1898) no person accused
of an offence under this Order in a trial before a Special Judge or convicted
and sentenced to imprisonment by such Judge for any offence shall be released
on bail or on his own bond unless the prosecution has been given an opportunity
to be heard in the matter.

Power of Government as to prosecution

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
12. Power of Government as to prosecution.--(1) No Court shall take cognizance of any
offence of hoarding or dealing in the back market except upon a complaint in
writing by or under the written authority of the Government.
(2) The Government may by order
direct that in case of clause trails (1) shall, other than trails before a
Special Judge the powers conferred upon it by
such circumstances, and under such conditions, if any, as may be
specified in the Order, be exercised by the District Magistrate.

Power to try summarily

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
13. Power to try summarily.-- Any Magistrate for the time being
empowered to try in a summary way the offences, specified in sub-section (1) of
section 260 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (V of 1898), may, if he
thinks fit, on application in his behalf by the prosecution and after hearing
the defence, try an offence of hoarding or dealing in
the Black Market in accordance with the provisions of sub-section (1) of
section 262 and Sections 263, 264 and 265 of the Code.

Appointment of Special Judge

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
14. Appointment of Special Judge.--(1) The Central Government shall
have power to appoint one or more Special Judges for the trial offences under
this Order.
(2) Any person may be appointed a
Special Judge who‑
(a) is or has been a Judge of High Court, or a Sessions Judge,
or
(b) is qualified to be appointed a Judge of the High Court.
(3) Every Special Judge shall be
appointed by the Central Government after consulting the High Court of West
Pakistan.

Cases triable by Special Judge

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
15. Cases triable by Special Judge.--(1)
Every Special Judge shall try such cases under this Order as the Government may
from time to time appoint in this regard by notification in the official Gazette,
and notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any other enactment for the time
begin in before force, an any such case which at the date of a notification
under clause (2) is pending Court s, ion such date, be deemed to stand
transferred to the Special Judge concerned in accordance with the notification.
(2) The Government may by a like
notification transfer any such case from one Special Judge to another or
withdraw any case from a Special Judge, or make such notification in the
description of any case (whether in the name of any accused or in the charge
preferred or in an other manner) as it may think necessary.

Procedure and power of Special Judge

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
16. Procedure and power of Special Judge.--(1) A Special Judge may
take cognizance of a case without the accused being committed for trial, and in
trying the case he shall follow the procedure prescribed by the Code of Criminal
Procedure, 1898 (V of 1898), for the trial of warrant cases by Magistrates:
Provided for a
Special Judge shall not be bound to adjourn any trial for any purpose whatever,
unless such adjournments in his opinion necessary in the interest of justice:
Provided further
that notwithstanding anything in the aforesaid Court of Special judge may,
unless in his discretion otherwise decides and except where a case has been
transferred to him by the High Court on the ground that a fair and impartial
could not be had in the Court from which the case is transferred, act on evidence
already recorded by any Court of Special Judge or his predecessors in office.
(2) Save as provided in clause
(1), the provisions of the said Code, except the provisions of Sections 196-A
and of Chapter XXXIII, shall so far as they are not inconsistent with this
Order, apply to all proceedings of a Special Judge, and for the purposes of the
said provisions the Special Judge shall be deemed to be a Court of Session
trying cases without a jury, and a person conducting a prosecution before a
Special Judge shall deemed to be a Public Prosecutor.

Appeal and revision

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
17. Appeal and revision.--The High Court may exercise, so far as
they may be applicable, all the powers conferred by Chapters XXXI and XXXII of
the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898 (V of 1898), on a High Court, as if the
Special Judge were a Court of Session trying cases without a jury within the
local limits of the High Court.

Bar of certain jurisdiction

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
18. Bar of certain jurisdiction.--No Court other than a High Court
shall have authority to transfer any case from a Special Judge to any other
Court of Special Judge or to make any order under section 491 of the Code of
Criminal Procedure, 1898 (V of 1898) or save as provided in Article 17, have
any jurisdiction of any kind in respect of any proceedings of a Special Judge.

Burden of proof in certain cases

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
19. Burden of proof in certain cases.--When any person is tried for
an offence of hoarding or dealing in the black market and any question arises
whether he did any act or was in possession of anything with lawful authority
or under a permit, licence or other document
prescribed by or under any law for the time begin in force, the burden of
proving that he had such authority permit, licence or
other document shall lie on him.

Accused person to be a competent witness

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
20. Accused person to be a competent witness.--Notwithstanding
anything to the contrary in any enactment for the time being in force any
person charged with hoarding or dealing in the black market shall be a
competent witness in his own defence, and may give against
him or against any person charged together with him at the same trial:
Provided that--
(a) he shall not be called as a witness except at his own
request;
(b) his failure
to give evidence shall not be made the subject of any comment by the
prosecution or give rise to any presumption against him or against any person
charged together with him at the same trial;
(c) he shall
not be asked any question tending to show that, that he has committed or been
convicted of any offence other than the offence with which he is charged, or is
of bad character, unless--
(i) the proof that he has committed
or been convicted of such offence is admissible in evidence to show that he is
guilty of the offence with which he is charged, or
(ii) he is
personally or by his pleader asked questions of any witness for the prosecution
with a view to establishing his own good character or has given evidence of his
good character, or
(iii) he has given evidence in disproof of the charge made against
any other person charged together with him at the same trial.

Notice of conviction to be displayed

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
21. Notice of conviction to be displayed.--(1) Upon the conviction
of any person for the offence of hoarding or dealing in the black market as the
case may be, the Government may require him to exhibit in or outside or both in
and outside his place of business (if any) notices of such number, size and
lettering, and placed in such positions and containing such particulars
relating to the convictions as it may determine and to keep them so exhibited
continuously for a period of not less than three months from the date of
conviction, and if he fails to comply fully with the requirement he shall be
deemed to have committed a further offence or hoarding or dealing in the black
market as the case may be, according to the nature of the original offence for
which he was convicted.
(2) If any person so convicted
refuses of fails to comply with any such requirement, any officer authorised in that behalf by any order of the Government in
writing may, without prejudice to any proceedings which may be brought in
respect of any such refusal of failure, affix the such person in accordance
with the requirement of the Government pursuance of the last preceding clause.
(3) Any person who obstructs any
such officer in exercise of any power conferred by clause (2) shall be
punishable with imprisonment either description for a term which may extend to
two years or with fine or with both.
(4) In any case the Government is
satisfied that the exhibition of notices in accordance with the requirements of
the foregoing provisions of this section will not effectively bring the
conviction to the notice of persons dealing with the convicted person, the
Government may in lieu of or in addition to any such requirement, require the
convicted person to exhibit for such period not being a period of less than
three months, on such stationery used in his business as may be specified in
the requirement, a notice placed in such position and printed in type of such
size and found and containing such particulars relating to the conviction as
may be specified in the requirement, and if he fails to comply fully with the
requirement he shall be deemed to have committed a further offence of hoarding
or dealing in the black market, as the case may be, according to the nature of
the original offence for which he was convicted.
sections.punishment:
punishable with imprisonment either description for a term which may extend to
two years or with fine or with both.

sections.description:
Powers to publish conviction

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
22. Powers to publish conviction.--If the Government is satisfied
that it is necessary so to do, the conviction and the particulars relating to
the conviction of any person for an offence under this Order may be published
in the Official Gazette.

Indemnity

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
23. Indemnity.--No suit, prosecution or legal proceeding whatever
shall lie against any public servant in respect of anything which is in good
faith done or intended to be done under this Order.

Except as otherwise provided

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
24. Except as otherwise
provided in this Order imprisonment for any offence under this Order shall
be rigorous.

Rule making power

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
25. Rule making power.--The Central Government may make rules for
carrying out the purposes of this Order.

Repeal

HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
HOARDING & BLACK MARKET ORDER, 1956
(PRESIDENT ORDER)
(ACT XIV OF 1956)
[22nd September, 1956]
26. Repeal.--The Hoarding and Black Market Act, 1948 (XXXIX of
1948), in the application to the Federal Capital, is hereby repealed.
